$comment: MCP tool contract for `elicit`. inputSchema/outputSchema are what the server advertises in its tool catalog. Single stance-blind pass surfacing the assumed objective and the governing preferences traced to their signals. Surfaces only - no enforcement. BASELINE, captured from the derived schemas at 038 rather than authored ahead of the code - this tool shipped without a contract, so there is no earlier statement of intent to restore. Its value starts now: any change to the Rust types fails the contract test until this file is updated deliberately.
name: elicit

inputSchema.description: Tool input: the task plus optional neutral context.

context.description: Optional neutral context — the only extra caller-prose input.

anyOf.description:
How much reasoning a call site should spend (022).

Maps to the provider's `output_config.effort`. It governs *all* output
tokens, thinking included, and is a behavioural signal rather than a hard
token budget — `MAX_TOKENS` remains the ceiling.

Unset is not `High`: an unset call site sends no `effort` field at all, so
the request body is byte-identical to before this feature. The provider's
own default is `high`, so unset and `High` behave the same, but only unset
is provably unchanged on the wire.

oneOf.description: Minimal reasoning; thinking skipped on simple tasks.
Moderate reasoning; thinking may be skipped on simple queries.
Deep reasoning on complex tasks. The provider's default.
Always thinks, no constraint on depth.
Always thinks deeply, with extended exploration.

effort.description:
Reasoning effort for this call alone. Omit to use the deployment's
configured level. Not every model family accepts this; when one rejects
it the error names the model, the level, and the remedies.

Typed rather than a free string so the accepted levels appear in the
published schema — the consumer of this server is a model reading that
schema, and a prose-only list is not something it can be constrained by.

task.description: What the caller is about to do, stated neutrally.

inputSchema.title: ElicitParams

DivergencePoint.description: One divergence point — server-zipped from the parallel arrays.

question.description: The assumption worth resolving, as a question.

GoverningPreference.description: One governing preference — server-zipped from the parallel arrays.

outputSchema.description: The aggregated tool output (data-model.md) — surfacing only, no enforcement.

divergence_points.description: The divergence points (empty when signals are consistent).

governing_preferences.description: The governing preferences (may be empty — low signal).

memory_consulted.description: Whether stored preferences were consulted (memory configured).

oneOf.description: Little/no preference signal — return few or none, fabricate nothing.

outputSchema.title: ElicitResult
